claim: LLMs frequently fail to abstain on unanswerable, underspecified, false-premise, subjective or stale questions, abstention does not improve with model scale, and reasoning fine-tuning makes it worse: reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, s1.1-32B) abstain markedly less than their own instruct base models (~24% average relative drop) even as their accuracy rises.

paper.title: AbstentionBench: Reasoning LLMs Fail on Unanswerable Questions
paper.s2_batch_record_title: AbstentionBench: Reasoning LLMs Fail on Unanswerable Questions

experiment.location_in_paper: Sec. 3 (datasets, models, judge), Sec. 4.1 (Figs. 2-4), 4.2 (Fig. 5 Tulu stages), 4.3 (Figs. 6-8 reasoning), 4.4 system prompt; App. C-D
experiment.task_or_benchmark: AbstentionBench: 20 datasets / 31 subsets over 6 scenarios (answer unknown, underspecified context, underspecified intent, false premise, subjective, stale) incl. new GSM8K-Abstain, GPQA-Abstain, MMLU-Math-Abstain, plus UMWP, FreshQA, MediQ, KUQ, CoCoNot, SelfAware, etc.
experiment.intervention_or_prompts: Default: no special system prompt, temperature 0.8, up to 4k tokens; reasoning models get 4k thinking tokens then forced final answer; reasoning-budget sweep 512-4096; abstention-encouraging system prompt ablation.
experiment.evaluation_procedure: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct judge decides abstention (88% accuracy vs human labels on GPT-4o/Llama-70B sample) and correctness of non-abstentions; per-sample abstention labels.
experiment.metric: Abstention recall (primary), precision, F1; response accuracy.
experiment.main_comparison: Across models/scale; post-training stages (base->SFT->DPO->RLVR); reasoning model vs its instruct base; reasoning budget; system prompt.
experiment.main_result: Abstention recall varies from near-perfect (BIG-Bench Known Unknowns) to near-zero (MediQ); no model dominates; Llama 3.1 8B->70B->405B shows almost no change in mean abstention. Tulu RLVR stage degrades abstention; SFT hurts underspecified-context abstention. Reasoning fine-tuning degrades abstention by 24% on average (abstract), on all datasets for both pairs incl. math/science; increasing s1.1 reasoning budget raises accuracy but not abstention. System prompt boosts abstention. My recomputation from the released analysis/abstention_performance.csv (unweighted mean over 31 subsets): R1-Distill-Llama-70B 0.475 vs Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct 0.668 recall; S1.1-32B 0.441 vs Qwen2.5-32B 0.731; reasoning worse on 29/31 subsets for each pair.

downstream.title: The Hallucination Tax of Reinforcement Finetuning
downstream.summary: Song, Shi, Zhao (concurrent, independent): standard RL fine-tuning for reasoning reduces refusal on unanswerable synthetic math problems by >80%; adding 10% unanswerable data restores refusal (abstract read).

downstream.title: Answering the Unanswerable Is to Err Knowingly: Analyzing and Mitigating Abstention Failures in Large Reasoning Models
downstream.summary: Liu et al.: large reasoning models consistently fail to abstain on unanswerable math problems even though internal cognition recognizes the flaw; propose monitoring + inference-time intervention (abstract read).

downstream.title: Agentic Abstention: Do Agents Know When to Stop Instead of Act?
downstream.summary: In web/terminal agent settings, Qwen3-235B thinking vs instruct and GPT-5.4-mini reasoning efforts: more reasoning slightly improves earliest-point abstention but lowers overall abstention recall (Fig. 5 read); scaling improves overall recall (Fig. 7), partially contradicting the 'no scale effect' part in this setting.

downstream.title: Knowing When Not to Answer: Evaluating Abstention in Multimodal Reasoning Systems
downstream.summary: MM-AQA: frontier VLMs rarely abstain under standard prompting; argues bottleneck is miscalibration rather than reasoning depth (abstract read).

downstream_summary: Independent work finds RL/reasoning fine-tuning suppresses refusal on unanswerable problems (Hallucination Tax; Liu et al.), and agentic follow-ups find more reasoning does not raise overall abstention. The 'no scale effect' sub-claim is less settled (an agentic benchmark finds scaling helps overall recall). Only ~15 months old, so still young.
notability_notes: NeurIPS 2025 D&B; FAIR; widely cited quickly (Semantic Scholar 137; paperclip listing showed 79) and adopted as an abstention benchmark in 2026 papers.
gaps: Overlaps with the reasoning topic (reasoning models' failure modes) - flag for dedup. First public 2025-06-10 (meets <=2026-03-29 cutoff). LLM-judge (Llama 3.1 8B) is 88% accurate; results depend on it. Paper's 24% figure aggregation not exactly reproduced.
